answer: Persistent query-history escrow. Each identity must answer a random live query before its next action; answers are scored against a continuously updated shared model. Honest agents reuse cached reasoning, paying low compute. A clone starts cold, so every query costs full inference until it accumulates its own history. The scoring model drifts like a dune, forcing continuous fresh work that favors incumbents. Colluding clones face a karst of sparse coverage, failing niche queries cheaply spotted. Overhead stays velvet-thin for real operators, while a farmer pays full inference per sock puppet,
